subsystems.name: Entangled photon source
subsystems.role: produces pairs of correlated photons whose properties are linked.
parts: nonlinear crystal for spontaneous parametric down-conversion

subsystems.name: Signal arm
subsystems.role: sends one photon of each pair to illuminate the scene and collects the returning light without spatial resolution.

subsystems.name: Idler arm
subsystems.role: detects the partner photon that never interacts with the scene, recording its position.
parts: spatially resolving single-photon detector (e.g. EMCCD or SPAD array)

subsystems.name: Correlation and reconstruction unit
subsystems.role: combines the two detection streams to form an image of the scene.

subsystems.name: Security analysis layer
subsystems.role: interprets the reconstructed image or correlation changes to detect an intruder.
parts: encryption or authentication of the photon stream

buildSteps.title: Generate entangled photons
buildSteps.detail: A pump laser is directed into a nonlinear crystal, where spontaneous parametric down-conversion creates pairs of photons with correlated momentum and position.

buildSteps.title: Separate signal and idler paths
buildSteps.detail: Beam splitters and filters route one photon of each pair along the signal arm (towards the scene) and the other along the idler arm (to a spatial detector).

buildSteps.title: Illuminate the scene with signal photons
buildSteps.detail: The signal photons are directed at the area to be monitored; any object present scatters or reflects some of them.

buildSteps.title: Collect returning signal photons
buildSteps.detail: A bucket detector gathers the reflected signal photons but does not resolve where they came from.

buildSteps.title: Detect idler photons spatially
buildSteps.detail: The idler photons, which have not touched the scene, are measured by a spatially resolving single-photon detector that records their positions.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the image
buildSteps.detail: Coincidence counting or computational correlation between the two detectors builds an image of the scene, even though the detected idler photons never interacted with it.

buildSteps.title: Apply security logic
buildSteps.detail: Algorithms compare successive reconstructed images or correlation statistics to flag changes caused by an intruder or an attempt to intercept the photon stream.

prerequisites.why: spontaneous parametric down-conversion is routinely used in labs, but sources are not yet ruggedised or compact for field security systems.
SPAD arrays and EMCCDs exist, but large-format, high-efficiency, low-noise arrays suitable for real-time ghost imaging are still developing.
demonstrated in laboratory settings, but real-time reconstruction under daylight or in cluttered environments remains difficult.
no fielded system combines quantum ghost imaging with practical perimeter or intrusion detection.

pathway.milestone: Laboratory demonstrations of ghost imaging with entangled photons and basic change detection
pathway.unlocks: proof that non-interacting photons can reveal a scene.

pathway.milestone: Field trials in controlled, dark or shielded environments for perimeter monitoring
pathway.unlocks: data on reliability, false alarms and operating conditions.

pathway.milestone: Integration with classical security cameras and alarm systems to cover gaps where conventional imaging struggles
Ruggedised, turnkey quantum ghost imaging sensors if cost and complexity fall
pathway.unlocks: deployment in niche high-security settings where stealth and low-light operation matter.
